name: Quiet Mind
description: Meditative study music for headphones: slow, soft pieces for long sessions of reading, writing and thinking, each using the space between your ears to settle the mind. An alpha beat under a singing bowl, sparse theta piano with rain beyond the glass, a pad that breathes from the centre of your head to all around it, brightness drifting between the ears, a drone rolling slowly inside your head, two hands that trade ears, strings that drift apart in cents, a harp that widens bar by bar, a phrase hidden in soft noise, a quiet beta lantern for alert focus and a delta music box to put the pens down. Each sketch is a complete piece of three to five minutes, with an intro, sections that come and go, a gentle ritardando and an ending that stops on its own: about fifty minutes in all. Slow tempos, low levels and nothing sudden; each sketch explains its trick in the comments. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Settling In
sketches.description: The start of a session, about five minutes long: a soft D major pad that breathes over eight bars, a singing bowl every four bars and wide, quiet air, over a 10 Hz binaural drone in the alpha range. High glass notes appear while you go deeper, and the piece eases to rest on a single chord. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.

sketches.name: Theta Notes
sketches.description: Deep reading, about five minutes long: a sparse, seeded piano that draws new phrases on every pass, soft chords in D minor and rain beyond the window, over a quiet 6 Hz binaural beat in the theta range. The piano rests for a moment in the margin, and the piece slows to a close. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.

sketches.name: Breathing Room
sketches.description: Nearly five minutes of slow breathing. A pad in C arrives in the centre of your head, then steps through the interaural phase: at 90 degrees it loosens and at 180 it spreads into a haze around you, where it stays for a while before coming back. A soft rush of air guides one slow breath every ten seconds, lengthening at the end. On speakers the 180-degree chords nearly vanish.

sketches.name: Paper and Ink
sketches.description: Writing at a desk, a little over four minutes: nothing is panned, yet the brightness of a soft broken-chord figure drifts slowly from ear to ear, as each ear has its own low-pass sweeping the other way every eight bars. A second draft plays the figure backwards, a pause lets the room settle, and the revision moves to B flat before coming home. A fire crackles on your left and a clock ticks on your right.

sketches.name: Slow Orbit
sketches.description: About five minutes: a drone whose phase turns slowly between the ears, from once every five seconds to just under once a second, so it rolls gently inside your head, under a hushed choir. Glass notes circle you once every sixteen bars, with new notes on their second orbit; in the still middle and at the end the drone barely turns. All rates stay well below 3 Hz.

sketches.name: Two Hands, Two Ears
sketches.description: About four minutes of generative piano in A minor pentatonic: two hands share one seeded melody, one leaning into each ear through a level difference, and every four bars they trade places. Each pass draws a new melody; the left hand begins and ends alone, and both rest in the middle while a held fifth and a distant stream keep the room still. Change the seed for a new take.

sketches.name: Cents of Calm
sketches.description: About four minutes: strings in G whose ears drift a few cents apart and back again (2 cents beats slowly, 4 shimmers and 8 widens softly around you) under a kalimba that plays a slow figure, the same in both ears. The strings begin alone, drift on their own in the middle, and the kalimba returns an octave higher before the close.

sketches.name: Widening Harp
sketches.description: About four minutes: a harp rolls slow broken chords in C while a delay between the ears, rising from 1 to 20 milliseconds, keeps it on one side but widens it bar by bar. A flute sings in the centre with no delay at all, an octave lower on its second verse, and rain falls outside as the harp slows to a close.

sketches.name: Quiet Signal
sketches.description: About five minutes of soft breaths of white noise that, between the ears, carry a slow phrase (Huggins pitch); each ear alone hears only hiss. A quiet sine plays the first phrase every four bars during the guided pass so you know what to listen for, then leaves you to hear it alone, over a soft pad and a singing bowl. The effect is faint and differs between listeners.

sketches.name: Beta Lantern
sketches.description: Four minutes of alert, steady focus in three passes: a gentle marimba figure in A minor and a soft kick over a pad that sends alternate partials to each ear, complete only when both ears hear it, with a very quiet 14 Hz binaural drone in the beta range. Between passes the marimba and kick rest for a lift; later passes play the figure backwards. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.

sketches.name: Pens Down
sketches.description: The end of the session, about three minutes: a music box in 3/4 floating a little above your head, over a 2 Hz binaural drone in the delta range, below the rates that trigger a pulse warning, with warm brown noise and crickets far away. After a hush the music box winds down to half speed, and the room slows into quiet.
